parts.label: (a)
parts.stem:
In aqueous solution, iodide ions react with acidified hydrogen peroxide, as shown in reaction 1.

reaction 1 $$2\text{I}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O}_2 + 2\text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{I}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

The rate equation for reaction 1 is shown.

$$\text{rate} = k[\text{I}^-][\text{H}_2\text{O}_2]$$

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by order of reaction.

parts.label: (a)(ii)

parts.label: (a)(iii)
(b)
parts.stem:
Nitrogen dioxide, $\text{NO}_2$, reacts with ozone, $\text{O}_3$, as shown in reaction 2.

reaction 2 $$2\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_3 \rightarrow \text{O}_2 + \text{N}_2\text{O}_5$$

The rate equation for reaction 2 is shown.

$$\text{rate} = k[\text{NO}_2][\text{O}_3]$$

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Two experiments are carried out to measure the rate of reaction 2.

In the first experiment, the initial rate is measured starting with known concentrations of $\text{NO}_2$ and $\text{O}_3$. In the second experiment, the concentrations of $\text{NO}_2$ and $\text{O}_3$ are **both** increased by a factor of four.

Predict how the initial rate for reaction 2 would change.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The reaction mechanism for reaction 2 has two steps.

Define rate-determining step.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Suggest equations for the **two** steps of the reaction mechanism for reaction 2.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem:
Dinitrogen pentoxide, $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$, can decompose to $\text{NO}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$.

The rate equation for this decomposition is shown.

$$\text{rate} = k[\text{N}_2\text{O}_5]$$

Fig. 4.2 shows the graph of rate against $[\text{N}_2\text{O}_5]$ for this decomposition.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

Fig. 4.2

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Use Fig. 4.2 to calculate a value for the rate constant, $k$, for this decomposition.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Use your answer to **(c)(i)** to calculate the half-life, $t_{\frac{1}{2}}$, in seconds, for this decomposition.
